title: This Rat Wears a Poison Strong Enough to Fell an Elephant

scenes.text: One bite of this rat can stop a predator's heart.
It's the African crested rat: rabbit-sized, fluffy, in no hurry. And it makes no poison of its own.
It borrows it. The rat chews the bark of the poison arrow tree, the same tree hunters used to tip their arrows.
Then it licks the toxic spit into a strip of special porous hairs along its sides, which soak it up.
Threatened, it doesn't run. It lifts its crest and parts its fur to show black and white stripes, right where the poison sits.
scenes.keywords: black and white striped fur animal

scenes.text: A few milligrams of that toxin can kill a person. No other mammal is known to arm itself with a plant's poison, and nobody knows how the rat survives it.

description:
The African crested rat chews the bark of the poison arrow tree, Acokanthera schimperi, and licks the toxin into specialised hairs on its flanks. A predator that bites gets a mouthful of heart-stopping cardenolides.
Researchers in Kenya trapped 25 of the rabbit-sized rats and watched 10 of them anoint themselves; it is the only mammal known to borrow a plant's poison for defence. The University of Utah team notes the poison can fell an elephant and a few milligrams can kill a human.
Which animal has the smartest defence?
subject: African crested rat
first_comment: The same study found these rats live in pairs and spend about half their time close together. Which poisonous animal should we cover next?
